meta.description: Applies ACMG/AMP 2015 framework with ClinGen SVI specifications, Tavtigian 2018/2020 Bayesian point system, Abou Tayoun 2018 PVS1 decision tree, Pejaver 2022 and Bergquist 2025 calibrated PP3/BP4 thresholds for REVEL/BayesDel/AlphaMissense, Brnich 2020 PS3/BS3 OddsPath, Walker 2023 SpliceAI splicing framework, and AMP/ASCO/CAP 2017 tumor tiers. Use when classifying germline variants P / LP / VUS / LB / B, applying VCEP-specific CSpec rules, computing Whiffin BS1, or assigning cancer Tier I-IV per Li 2017.

scientific_integrity.detail: The retained execution did not fabricate patient results, studies, sample sizes, p-values, or treatment effects; observed values came from candidate calls, bounded controls, or cited primary guidance.

practice_boundaries.detail: The executable emits definitive germline and somatic classification labels without a required non-diagnostic boundary, qualified clinical review, or explicit prohibition on patient-specific treatment decisions.

methodological_ground.detail: The candidate materially mis-maps Brnich PS3/BS3 OddsPath strengths, ignores disease-transcript relevance in PVS1, shortcuts splice PVS1, and applies unsupported AlphaMissense evidence inside the calibrated indeterminate interval.

code_usability.detail: The advertised live GeneBe helper uses a removed HGVS-style request contract and consistently receives HTTP 400 from the reachable current API; the supplied CSpec route also returns HTTP 400.

functional_suitability.note: The skill covers many promised evidence classes, but the load-bearing PVS1, OddsPath, AlphaMissense, GeneBe, and CSpec paths do not implement their advertised current methods.

reliability.note: Deterministic helpers are present, but invalid domains, unknown codes, duplicate evidence, stale services, and zero penetrance are not handled safely or actionably.

performance_context.note: The concise main skill routes detail to one reference and one script; the long reference repeats some tables and claims but remains conditionally loaded.

agent_usability.note: Authority order and workflow are readable, but executable outputs omit required context, conflict handling, validation, and a reliable current-interface path.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers and tables are discoverable, while definitive clinical labels and stale links make ordinary use insufficiently forgiving.

security.note: No credentials or raw-code execution are present, but clinically consequential inputs are unsanitized and no protected-health-data or patient-use boundary is stated.

maintainability.note: The single script is readable and modular, but method constants lack source-linked regression tests and several accepted parameters are unused or weakly typed.

agent_specific.note: Triggering and progressive disclosure are adequate; deterministic composition is undermined by silent unknown-code acceptance, duplicate counting, and missing stop conditions for clinical use.

inputs.label: Default BRCA1-style demonstration
inputs.note: The script exited zero but summed discordant REVEL and SpliceAI evidence plus an over-strengthened PS3 call into a precise Likely Pathogenic result without required interpretation context.

assertions.text: The documented standalone command executes and reports retained criteria, points, and category.
assertions.note: It exited zero and printed four criteria, eight points, and Likely Pathogenic.

assertions.text: Functional OddsPath 8.0 is mapped to the Brnich Moderate strength.
assertions.note: The helper returned PS3 Strong instead of PS3 Moderate.

assertions.text: Discordant computational evidence is reconciled instead of blindly summed.
assertions.note: PP3 Strong and BP4 Supporting were both retained and arithmetically combined.

assertions.text: The result records disease, transcript, VCEP, mechanism, assay validity, and uncertainty context.
assertions.note: None of those load-bearing fields appears in the output.

assertions.text: The output states a non-diagnostic clinical-use boundary and requires qualified review.
assertions.note: No medical or clinical-review boundary is printed.

inputs.label: PVS1 transcript relevance and escape branches
inputs.note: Three simple boundaries matched, but the helper ignored a false disease-relevant-transcript flag and assigned splice PVS1 Strong without determining the transcript consequence.

assertions.text: A relevant-transcript nonsense variant predicted to undergo NMD receives PVS1 Very Strong in the simplified branch.
assertions.note: The relevant-transcript control returned PVS1_VeryStrong.

assertions.text: Exactly ten percent and more than ten percent removed are distinguished at the documented boundary.
assertions.note: Exactly 0.10 returned Moderate and 0.100001 returned Strong.

assertions.text: A variant outside a biologically relevant disease transcript does not receive PVS1.
assertions.note: The ignored false flag still returned PVS1_VeryStrong.

assertions.text: Canonical splice variants require predicted or observed transcript consequence and rescue-transcript review before strength assignment.
assertions.note: A splice donor escaping NMD returned PVS1_Strong from booleans alone.

assertions.text: The callable contract enforces an established LoF disease mechanism before PVS1 application.
assertions.note: No gene-disease mechanism input or validation exists in the helper.

inputs.label: PS3 and BS3 OddsPath boundaries
inputs.note: Only 4 of 14 exact Brnich boundary expectations matched; pathogenic strengths were shifted upward, benign mirrors were misplaced, and PS3 Very Strong was absent.

assertions.text: The mapping is deterministic across exact and adjacent boundary values.
assertions.note: Repeated scalar calls returned stable code strings or null.

assertions.text: Pathogenic thresholds implement indeterminate through Very Strong exactly as Brnich Table 3 specifies.
assertions.note: The helper adds 1.2, shifts 2.1 and 4.3 strengths upward, and never emits Very Strong above 350.

assertions.text: Benign thresholds implement 0.48, 0.23, and 0.053 boundaries without over-strengthening.
assertions.note: Exact 0.48 was supporting and values near 0.23 and 0.053 were assigned Strong too early.

assertions.text: Reference prose and code agree on the evidence-strength names.
assertions.note: The reference calls greater than 18.7 Very Strong while the code returns the generic Strong code.

assertions.text: Invalid nonpositive OddsPath is rejected before assigning benign evidence.
assertions.note: Negative OddsPath was accepted as BS3 Strong.

inputs.label: Tavtigian endpoints and subsumption
inputs.note: The signed point endpoints and PVS1 subsumption were correct, but unknown criteria silently became zero points and duplicate evidence was counted twice.

assertions.text: Pathogenic, likely pathogenic, and VUS endpoints match 10, 6, and 0 to 5 points.
assertions.note: All checked positive and zero endpoints matched.

assertions.text: Likely benign and benign endpoints match -1 through -6 and at most -7.
assertions.note: The -1, -6, and -7 fixtures returned the documented categories.

assertions.text: PVS1 subsumes PP3 and PM4 when they represent the same mechanism.
assertions.note: PP3 Strong was removed and the retained PVS1 plus PM2 total was nine.

assertions.text: Unknown evidence codes fail explicitly instead of disappearing into a zero score.
assertions.note: NOT_A_CRITERION was retained in output but silently contributed zero.

assertions.text: Duplicate evidence codes are rejected or de-duplicated before summation.
assertions.note: Two PS3 strings were counted as eight points.

inputs.label: Bergquist AlphaMissense calibration
inputs.note: Only 3 of 11 calibrated boundary expectations matched; the helper assigned evidence at 0.2 and 0.7 inside the calibrated indeterminate band and cannot emit graded strengths.

assertions.text: The helper is deterministic and returns only documented evidence-code strings or null.
assertions.note: Every bounded scalar call returned a stable supporting code or null.

assertions.text: Scores from 0.170 through 0.791 remain indeterminate under the advertised Bergquist calibration.
assertions.note: The helper returned BP4 Supporting at 0.2 and PP3 Supporting at 0.7 and 0.791.

assertions.text: Pathogenic supporting evidence begins at the calibrated threshold near 0.792.
assertions.note: The implemented threshold begins at 0.7.

assertions.text: The implementation represents the advertised Moderate and Strong pathogenic evidence intervals.
assertions.note: All values at 0.906, 0.972, and 0.990 remained PP3 Supporting.

assertions.text: AlphaMissense inputs outside the probability domain are rejected.
assertions.note: Negative and greater-than-one scores were accepted and assigned evidence.

inputs.label: Germline-somatic separation and invalid inputs
inputs.note: Normal germline and somatic labels stayed separate, but invalid evidence, numeric domains, and somatic levels were accepted or crashed, and Tier III/IV remained collapsed.

assertions.text: Germline output uses P/LP/VUS/LB/B categories and somatic output uses Tier I-IV labels.
assertions.note: The normal fixtures returned separate classification vocabularies.

assertions.text: The five documented normal somatic branches remain independently reachable.
assertions.note: Tier I-A, I-B, II-C, II-D, and the combined III/IV fallback were observed.

assertions.text: Unknown and duplicate germline criteria are rejected before scoring.
assertions.note: Unknown evidence scored zero and duplicate PS3 scored twice.

assertions.text: Predictor, prevalence, penetrance, OddsPath, and somatic evidence domains are validated actionably.
assertions.note: Out-of-range and negative values were accepted, while zero penetrance raised a raw ZeroDivisionError.

assertions.text: Somatic Tier III and Tier IV are distinguishable and invalid levels cannot be promoted.
assertions.note: The helper collapses III/IV and mapped level -1 to Tier II-C.

inputs.label: Current GeneBe and CSpec interfaces
inputs.note: Both shipped routes returned HTTP 400, while the current GeneBe coordinate control and CSpec REST service/version controls returned HTTP 200.

assertions.text: The shipped GeneBe helper succeeds against the documented current public endpoint.
assertions.note: Its variant=HGVS request received HTTP 400 requiring chr, pos, ref, and alt.

assertions.text: A documented current GeneBe coordinate request succeeds and returns a parsed variant payload.
assertions.note: The bounded chr/pos/ref/alt/genome control returned HTTP 200 and variants.

assertions.text: The supplied CSpec authoritative registry URL succeeds for public GET access.
assertions.note: The candidate /cspec/ui/svi/all route returned an explicit invalid-URL HTTP 400.

assertions.text: Current CSpec REST service and versioned gene routes are publicly reachable.
assertions.note: Both /cspec/srvc and the GATM version endpoint returned HTTP 200 JSON.

assertions.text: The skill provides an actionable fallback when a public interface drifts.
assertions.note: The helper exposes a raw HTTP error and the reference points only to the stale route.

key_strengths: The normalized package preserves MIT provenance and uses clear progressive disclosure across the main skill, reference, and reusable script.
The Tavtigian signed point endpoints and PVS1 subsumption of PP3 and PM4 are implemented deterministically and matched the bounded endpoint fixtures.
The main workflow explicitly prioritizes VCEP CSpec over ClinGen SVI and generic ACMG and warns against stacking correlated missense predictors.
Germline ACMG categories and somatic AMP/ASCO/CAP tier labels are kept in separate callable paths.

recommendations.title: ACMG-001: Correct the OddsPath strength mapping
recommendations.problem: The helper shifts most pathogenic and benign OddsPath intervals to the wrong strength and cannot represent PS3 Very Strong above 350.
recommendations.root_cause: The reference and function encode a non-Brnich threshold table with an extra 1.2 pathogenic boundary and incorrect reciprocal mirrors.
recommendations.fix: Implement the exact Brnich Table 3 intervals, including the indeterminate range and PS3 Very Strong. Add exact-and-adjacent regressions for 0.053, 0.23, 0.48, 2.1, 4.3, 18.7, and 350, and align the reference table.

recommendations.title: ACMG-002: Enforce the complete PVS1 prerequisites
recommendations.problem: A false disease-relevant-transcript flag still produces PVS1 Very Strong, and splice variants receive a fixed strength without consequence or rescue-transcript review.
recommendations.root_cause: The sketch accepts transcript relevance but never evaluates it and reduces the decision tree to variant type plus a few booleans.
recommendations.fix: Return no PVS1 when the affected transcript or exon is not biologically relevant. Require established LoF disease mechanism, transcript consequence, NMD location, rescue-transcript/cryptic-splice review, and VCEP overrides; otherwise return an explicit review-required state.

recommendations.title: ACMG-003: Implement or stop claiming AlphaMissense calibration
recommendations.problem: The skill promises Bergquist 2025 graded calibration but uses unsupported 0.2 and 0.7 supporting-only cutoffs that classify indeterminate scores as evidence.
recommendations.root_cause: A conservative placeholder was retained after the frontmatter and reference were updated to the newer calibration.
recommendations.fix: Either implement the current calibrated intervals with source/version metadata and boundary tests or remove AlphaMissense scoring from the executable and route users to a verified current table. Reject values outside zero to one.

recommendations.title: ACMG-004: Update the GeneBe API contract
recommendations.problem: The shipped helper always receives HTTP 400 because the current single-variant GET requires genomic coordinate fields rather than variant=HGVS.
recommendations.root_cause: The wrapper targets an older public request shape and has no compatibility check or conversion step.
recommendations.fix: Accept and validate chr, pos, ref, alt, and genome for the current GET, or explicitly call a documented conversion endpoint before annotation. Parse the current response schema and add a mocked request contract plus bounded live smoke.

recommendations.title: ACMG-005: Replace the stale CSpec registry route
recommendations.problem: The authoritative URL documented throughout the candidate returns HTTP 400 as an invalid GET path.
recommendations.root_cause: A legacy UI route was treated as a stable API and no versioned lookup recipe was retained.
recommendations.fix: Document the current CSpec REST service and gene/specification version endpoints, require access date and selected version, and add a non-mutating reachability/schema smoke.

recommendations.title: ACMG-006: Validate evidence and numerical domains
recommendations.problem: Unknown and duplicate criteria, out-of-range predictors, negative OddsPath or prevalence, zero penetrance, and invalid somatic evidence can produce silent misclassification or raw exceptions.
recommendations.root_cause: The helpers use direct comparisons and dictionary get-with-zero without typed validation or evidence uniqueness rules.
recommendations.fix: Add typed finite-domain validation, require positive OddsPath and penetrance, bound probability scores, reject unknown codes, de-duplicate or reject repeated criteria, validate somatic evidence enums, and return actionable errors.

recommendations.title: ACMG-007: Rebuild the default example around an evidence trail
recommendations.problem: The demonstration sums discordant computational evidence and prints a precise category without the rule set, disease mechanism, transcript, VCEP, assay calibration, exclusions, or unresolved conflicts.
recommendations.root_cause: The example is a scalar helper showcase rather than the evidence-led clinical workflow described by the skill.
recommendations.fix: Use a synthetic explicitly non-clinical case with validated inputs, one selected predictor, exact OddsPath strength, conflict/exclusion reporting, rule-set version, and an uncertainty-first output schema.

recommendations.title: ACMG-008: Add a clinical practice boundary
recommendations.problem: The skill emits definitive variant classifications without requiring qualified clinical review or forbidding use as patient-specific diagnosis or treatment advice.
recommendations.root_cause: The documentation distinguishes frameworks but does not define a medical-use stop condition or review responsibility.
recommendations.fix: State that the helper is educational and not validated for clinical diagnosis, require expert review and current laboratory SOP/VCEP guidance, prohibit treatment decisions from the output alone, and avoid protected patient data in examples or logs.

recommendations.title: ACMG-009: Separate somatic Tier III and Tier IV
recommendations.problem: The somatic helper collapses VUS-somatic and benign-somatic and uses a loose numeric OncoKB surrogate.
recommendations.root_cause: The illustrative tier function lacks explicit validated evidence objects and benignity evidence.
recommendations.fix: Replace the scalar shortcut with explicit same-tumor, guideline, regulatory, investigational, and benignity evidence fields plus access dates, then return distinct Tier III and Tier IV states.
